614.t: Stravinsky's telegram and the Ebony Concerto premiere at Carnegie Hall

614.ch: Decca years and the First Herd

202.s: He recalls Herman's Stravinsky piece and Stokowski at NBC, then a fast string date requiring all afterbeats.

791.t: Einstein's Red/Blue Universe at Carnegie Hall
791.s: Her first piece for symphony orchestra with brass moving in the balconies, and the nervous premiere.
791.q: Yeah. That was like a further incarnation of some of that NASA work. Basically that was a piece called “Einstein’s Red/Blue Universe,” and it was played by The American Composers Orchestra, a very fine new music orchestra in New York, conducted by Dennis Russell Davies, and it was my first piece…

792.t: Stravinsky rehearses the Ebony Concerto with the Herman band
792.s: Chubby shows his book The Happy Monster, then recounts rehearsing with Stravinsky, the photo with the bass, the Carnegie Hall success and Baltimore booing.
792.ch: Bass craft and the Herman band
792.q: Well it’s very difficult. Because it’s really nuts. I mean the guy took a picture and I’ve always been this. I did a dumb thing. Igor Stravinsky came up to the Paramount Theater backstage, to rehearse the Ebony Concerto, and this is wild, it really is—

793.t: Playing in Frank Zappa's symphony piece in Berkeley
793.s: She played sax in a very difficult Zappa work commissioned by the Berkeley symphony; the dress rehearsal featured a puppet show that shocked a friend's parents, and the orchestra lost money.
793.q: Yes. The Berkley, California Symphony commissioned him. This is a great story. They commissioned him to write a symphony or whatever. And in my opinion he listened to all the modern cats and then he brought in this — actually I was playing saxophone with it, and I had never — excuse me — played…

523.t: Symphonic challenges: Villa-Lobos and 'The Rite of Spring'
523.s: Raph mentions recording 'Forest of the Amazon' with Villa-Lobos and playing bass trumpet in 'The Rite of Spring' with the Ridgefield Symphony.
523.q: Yeah. I recorded “Forest of the Amazon” with Villa Lobos and that had some moments. And there are a number of symphonic things. Yeah. There were moments, a lot of moments.

239.t: Conducting the Kalamazoo Symphony for Erroll Garner
239.s: Jones conducted the one symphony date for Garner, who lagged his right hand, so he conducted ahead of the orchestra.
239.q: So he wanted to play it safe, because he's told me that a lot of the guys just lag all the time, you know, they make the orchestra lag and lose the tempo.
